strategies.title: Minimal v2 Migration
strategies.rationale: Smallest complete migration updating dependency pin, model config, validators, and serialization/parsing methods to v2 equivalents while preserving all public behavior.
ordered_steps: Convert models.py Config class to model_config dict with from_attributes=True, replace anystr_strip_whitespace with str_strip_whitespace, change Field(alias=) to Field(validation_alias=)
Replace @validator with @field_validator and @root_validator with @model_validator, update signatures to use ValidationInfo
Replace parse_obj with model_validate, parse_raw with model_validate_json, dict() with model_dump() in api.py

strategies.title: Compatibility Layer Migration
strategies.rationale: Maintains v1 method aliases (parse_obj, parse_raw, dict) alongside v2 natives, wraps ValidationError for test compatibility, and uses dual-config pattern for gradual adoption.
ordered_steps: In models.py: define model_config dict with from_attributes=True and str_strip_whitespace=True; keep Config class as deprecated alias; use Field(validation_alias=) with alias= deprecated param
Decorate validators with @field_validator/@model_validator but also attach v1-style @validator wrappers that delegate to new validators for backward compatibility

In api.py: keep parse_user/serialize_user/parse_project_json signatures but implement via model_validate/model_validate_json/model_dump; add try/except to re-raise ValidationError from pydantic_core if needed

strategies.title: Full Refactor to v2 Idioms
strategies.rationale: Adopts v2-native patterns: Annotated fields for validation, model_config as dict, @field_validator/@model_validator with ValidationInfo, and removes all v1-isms for cleaner long-term maintenance.
ordered_steps: Rewrite models.py: replace Field with Annotated[Type, Field(...)] for alias/validation_alias; model_config = {'from_attributes': True, 'str_strip_whitespace': True}; validators use @field_validator(mode='before')/@model_validator with info: ValidationInfo
Remove Config class entirely; convert root_validator to @model_validator with skip_on_failure via info.context

In api.py: rename parse_user -> validate_user, serialize_user -> dump_user, parse_project_json -> validate_project_json; implement directly with model_validate/model_validate_json/model_dump; update type hints to v2 BaseModel

citations.title: Migration Guide | Pydantic Docs
citations.evidence: Some of the built-in data-loading functionality has been slated for removal. In particular, `parse_raw` and `parse_file` are now deprecated. In Pydantic V2, `model_validate_json` works like `parse_raw`. Otherwise, you should load the data and then pass it to `model_validate`. The `from_orm` method has been deprecated; you can now just use `model_validate` (equivalent to `parse_obj` from Pydantic V1) to achieve something similar, as long as you’ve set `from_attributes=True` in the model config. The `__eq__` method has changed for models. + Models can only be equal to other `BaseModel` instances. + For two model instances to be equal, they must have the same: - Type (or, in the case of generic models, non-parametrized generic origin type) - Field values [...] #### Changes to `@validator`’s allowed signatures In Pydantic V1, functions wrapped by `@validator` could receive keyword arguments with metadata about what was being validated. Some of these arguments have been removed from `@field_validator` in Pydantic V2: `config`: Pydantic V2’s config is now a dictionary instead of a class, which means this argument is no longer backwards compatible. If you need to access the configuration you should migrate to `@field_validator` and use `info.config`. `field`: this argument used to be a `ModelField` object, which was a quasi-internal class that no longer exists in Pydantic V2. Most of this information can still be accessed by using the field name from `info.field_name` to index into
